newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EUROPEAN BATTLES MARK END OF SOCCER'S WINTER HIBERNATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EUROPEAN BATTLES MARK END OF SOCCER'S WINTER HIBERNATION.

text.p: The TV presenters are taking their smart blazers out of the wardrobe, the statisticians are getting their facts right and the couch potatoes are buying in the beer to welcome back the return of European soccer competition after its three-month winter hibernation.

The more adventurous fans -- and the ones who can afford it -- are jumping on planes and trains and driving across the borders to see their teams in action, typified by a huge army of Danes en route to remote Tenerife in the Canaries to see Brondby take on the Spanish side in the UEFA Cup.
All three competitions resume with the first legs of the quarter-finals with Italy, England, France and Spain still in with a chance of achieving a clean sweep of the trophies.

Juventus resume their bid to keep the European Cup in Turin when they visit surprise quarter-finalists Rosenborg Trondheim on Wednesday, while Fiorentina travel to Benfica for a Cup Winners Cup match and Inter Milan face Anderlecht in the UEFA Cup.

England's three-pronged attack features Manchester United, who entertain Portugese champions Porto at home in the European Cup, Liverpool, who face Brann Bergen in the Cup Winners Cup and depleted Newcastle, suffering with injuries and a suspension for Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla, against French league leaders Monaco at St James' Park.

France's bid for a rare European trophy rests not only with Monaco, but also with Auxerre, who face a tough task at Borussia Dortmund in the Champions Cup and Paris St Germain, who entertain AEK Athens in the Cup Winners Cup.
Atletico Madrid lead Spain's assault with an away first leg visit to last season's beaten finalists Ajax, while Barcelona face AIK Stockholm at home in the Cup Winners Cup.
Spain still have two clubs in the UEFA Cup with Tenerife at home to Brondby and Valencia away at Schalke in Germany.

Juventus fully expected to be playing arch-rivals AC Milan at this stage of the competition, until Milan were surprisingly eliminated by Rosenborg in the last round of matches in the Champions League.

Juventus now take on the Norwegian part-timers who have sold two of their key players since the Champions League phase ended in December with defender Bjorn Tore Kvarme moving to Liverpool and striker Steffen Iversen going to Tottenham.
It would be a major upset if Rosenborg eliminated Juventus over the two legs, even if Juventus are without some of their key players through injury like Alessandro Del Piero and Alen Boksic.

There are fascinating ties in prospect between Ajax and Atletico Madrid and Manchester United and Porto, who come to Old Trafford looking to become the third team to win a European tie there this season.

But while Manchester United's form has been consistently good in recent weeks, Porto's has fallen away. Although they are still 10 points clear of second-placed Sporting, they have recently lost their 30-match unbeaten league record and their players lost their control when an injury time penalty cost them victory in a league match against Amadora on Friday.
United, on the other hand, have moved to the top of the English league and opened up a four-point lead at the weekend when they beat Coventry and second-placed Liverpool lost at Aston Villa.
Porto coach Antonio Oliveira praised Manchester United before leaving for England on Monday.
"Manchester United are better and stronger than AC Milan," he said, referring to the former Italian champions whom Porto beat away in the league phase of the championship.
"United are without doubt the best team that we have met this season," he said. "We are going to need to be at our very best and inspired.
Another team looking for inspiration are Ajax who face Aletico Madrid hoping to salvage some honour out of their poorest season for years.
Dumped out of the domestic cup competition and trailing the Dutch league leaders PSV Eindhoven by 18 points, the European Cup offers Ajax the last big chance in what has been a miserable season.

Injuries before the winter break and a change in personnel from the team which swept to two consecutive European Cup finals in 1995 and 1996 have left Ajax flat, although the recent win against arch-rivals Feyenoord hinted at a return to form. But a lacklustre second half to the season and an unconvincing performance against Atletico Madrid could leave the Amsterdam side staring at the prospect of missing out on European competition for the first time since the early 1990s when they were barred for a year after a missile throwing incident.
